text.text_excerpt: I came here to grab dinner while my friends were passed out in the hotel room....it was a great surprise. The interior is very trendy and the menu is pretty unique compared to most restaurants I ate at while in New Orleans. I ordered the kale salad and pork belly. Both were very delicious with great presentation, and I thought were a decent sized portion. I left pleasantly full and happy with my meal. The bartender was also very nice.

It is tough to review this restaurant since every few months it changes again. The latest change is with a new chef and management team formerly at Marginy Brassiere (another restaurant that changes chefs every time the wind blows a different direction, but I'll save that for another review). Meson is a great modern space. Jerry Fertel (son of Ruth Fertel - Ruths' Chris Steakhouse) spent a small fortune renovating this former corner market/deli/convenience store into a beautiful restaurant. The space is modern and contemporary, while still feeling warm with a great use of beautiful wood tables and bar. I am a big fan of Coolinary season, and I try to take advantage of the various prix fixe menus offered to try restaurants I haven't visited before. Meson 923 has been in my bookmarks for quite some time. So with $35 in hand, here's what Chef Rabasa and Co. were kind enough to serve me: Cocktail of the day: Lemongrass infused vodka, lime juice, malibu coconut rum martini. I like the idea of infusing vodka with aromatics, because otherwise vodka is boring... for fratboys and alcoholics. Lemongrass plus coconut missed the mark for me, but my dining companion enjoyed it.
